etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English *printen, prenten, preenten, an apheretic form of emprinten, enprinten (“to impress; imprint”) (see imprint). Compare Dutch prenten (“to imprint”), Middle Low German prenten (“to print; write”), Danish prente (“to print”), Swedish prenta (“to write German letters”). Compare also Late Old French printer, preindre (“to press”), from Latin premere (“to press”).

definitions.definition: Of, relating to, or writing for printed publications.
(transitive) To produce one or more copies of a text or image on a surface, especially by machine; often used with out or off: print out, print off.
To produce a microchip (an integrated circuit) in a process resembling the printing of an image.
(transitive, intransitive) To write very clearly, especially, to write without connecting the letters as in cursive.
(transitive, intransitive) To publish in a book, newspaper, etc.

quote.citation: 1716, Alexander Pope, The Poetical Works of Alexander Pope, Preface:
quote.text: From the moment he prints, he must expect to hear no more truth.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To stamp or impress (something) with coloured figures or patterns.
(transitive) To fix or impress, as a stamp, mark, character, idea, etc., into or upon something.

quote.citation: c. 1547?, Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, Description of the Fickel Affections, Pangs, and Slights of Love:
quote.text: A look will print a thought that never may remove.
Upon his breastplate he beholds a dint, / Which in that field young Edward's sword did print.

quote.citation: 1701, Wentworth Dillon, 4th Earl of Roscommon, Silenus:
quote.text: some footsteps printed in the clay

definitions.definition: (transitive) To stamp something in or upon; to make an impression or mark upon by pressure, or as by pressure.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “Palamon and Arcite”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Forth on his fiery steed betimes he rode, / That scarcely prints the turf on which he trod.

definitions.definition: (computing, transitive) To display a string on the terminal.

quote.citation: 2010, Chuck Easttom, Advanced JavaScript, Jones & Bartlett Learning, →ISBN, page 217:
quote.text: However, when you print the string you can see only 11 characters (c, a, r, ', s,, w, h, e, e, l).

quote.citation: 2015, Othmar Kyas, How To Smart Home: A Step by Step Guide to Your Personal Internet of Things, Key Concept Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: On the RHS side we write the current date to the variable date and print it to the terminal window, followed by the string "Chris coming home...." .

definitions.definition: (finance, transitive, intransitive) To produce an observable value.
(transitive) To fingerprint (a person).

quote.text: Maybe we'll get lucky; maybe he was printed for some minor infraction in some backwater town.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) Books and other material created by printing presses, considered collectively or as a medium.
(uncountable) Clear handwriting, especially, writing without connected letters as in cursive.
(uncountable) The letters forming the text of a document.
(countable) A newspaper.

quote.text: I spent my second quarter-centuryLosing what I had learnt at universityAnd refusing to take in what had happened since.Now I know none of the names in the public prints  […]

definitions.definition: A visible impression on a surface.
A fingerprint.
A footprint.
(visual art) A picture that was created in multiple copies by printing.
(photography) A photograph that has been printed onto paper from the negative.
(film) A copy of a film that can be projected.
Cloth that has had a pattern of dye printed onto it.

quote.citation: 1838 (date written), L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], “(please specify the page)”, in Lady Anne Granard; or, Keeping up Appearances. […], volume I, London: Henry Colburn, […], published 1842, →OCLC, pages 20–21:
quote.text: The poor are very unreasonable; a kind look and word often go farther in winning upon their affection than even a piece of coarse flannel, or a remnant of dark print.

definitions.definition: (architecture) A plaster cast in bas relief.
(finance) A datum.

quote.citation: 2023, Ilia Bouchouev, Virtual Barrels : Quantitative Trading in the Oil Market, Springer, →ISBN, page 150:
quote.text: The reference index is calculated using monthly CPI prints but with a lag of between two and three months.
